types.necessity: L1.identity says a customer is the thing the brokerage already identifies by a customer number, and a change never makes it a different customer; a stable identifier value is what lets two rows be recognized as the same customer.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible as long as the brokerage's customer number is never reused for a different customer; review if a customer number is ever reassigned.
types.review_trigger: business reports a reused customer number

types.necessity: L1.identity says an account is the thing the brokerage already identifies by an account number, and a change never makes it a different account; a stable identifier value is what lets two rows be recognized as the same account.

types.review_trigger: business reports a reused account number

types.necessity: L1.history requires every change to a customer to be kept with the moment it took effect, and L1.as-of requires answering any question as of a moment by finding the statement in effect then; both require a statement to carry the moment it took effect.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible where the source states its own moment of effect; review wherever a source does not (see L1.hole.change-effective-time).
types.review_trigger: business restates what moment a change takes effect at

types.necessity: L1.current-version says the current statement about a customer is the one with no later statement, and there is exactly one; a flag computed from that test is what makes 'current' answerable without re-deciding it ad hoc.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible as long as statements for one customer are totally ordered by effective time; review if two statements ever claim the same effective moment.
types.review_trigger: an as-of query returns zero or more than one current statement

types.necessity: L1.history keeps a dated statement about a customer; without any content beyond identity and time, that statement answers nothing about how the customer stood, so it must carry the one fact the source itself names for a customer's standing.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible as long as the source's action-code and status-code meanings are the only stated content for how a customer stood; review if the business names additional standing content.
types.review_trigger: business defines additional content for a customer statement

types.necessity: L1.owner-standing says an account's standing includes its owner's standing at the same moment; naming which customer that is, per statement, is what makes the join to the customer's own statement possible.

entities.necessity: L1.history requires every change to a customer to be kept beside the earlier statement rather than overwritten; L1.as-of requires that any question about a customer be answerable as of a moment; L1.current-version requires exactly one current statement. invariants.necessity: L1.constructed-scenarios requires that a constructed scenario never introduce an account the brokerage does not have; this is a direct, checkable restatement of that requirement.

invariants.review_trigger: a ce.account_changes row names an account_id absent from every raw.-sourced statement
invariants.statement: Every account_id carried by a ce.account_changes-sourced handoff already appears among account_id values carried by raw.-sourced handoffs.

holes.question: When a customer's standing changes, does the brokerage consider every account of that customer to also receive a new statement at that same moment, or only the customer? This determines whether account versioning must also be triggered by customer-only change events, in addition to account-subject actions.

Incremental customer and account change records carry no event time of their own, only a load batch_date. Does such a change take effect at the file's batch date, or at some other moment the source does not state?
Incremental files can mark a customer or account record deleted (cdc_flag = D). What does that mean for the kept history, current statement, and as-of answers of the customer or account it names?

sufficiency_groups.coverage_claim: The identifier types and attributes, fed by every historical and incremental source that carries a customer or account number, give every statement a stable identity so two rows sharing that number are recognized as the same customer or account across all changes, exactly as L1.identity requires.

The versioned customer entity keeps every historical change as its own dated, contentful statement; the current flag and invariants make the current statement, non-overlap, and unique as-of answer directly checkable. Historical action-log changes are fully covered. Incremental changes' content (status) is covered the same way, but their effective time is not, since the incremental source states no moment of its own.

The versioned account entity keeps every historical change as its own dated, contentful statement; the current flag and invariants make the current statement, non-overlap, and unique as-of answer directly checkable. Historical action-log changes are fully covered. Incremental changes' content (status) is covered the same way, but their effective time is not, since the incremental source states no moment of its own.

The owner reference attribute, fed whenever an account statement's source names its customer, lets any account statement be joined to its customer's statement at the same moment, and the invariant states that the account's as-of answer must include that joined customer answer, which is what L1.owner-standing requires. Whether the reverse also holds -- that a customer-only change alone must mint a new account statement -- is not decided by the clause and is carried as a deferred, unresolved member.

No handoff or attribute here resolves what a deleted (cdc_flag = D) customer change record means for kept history; the sole member names that the question is open, so L1.history's 'nothing is overwritten' guarantee is not claimed for deleted rows.

No handoff or attribute here resolves what a deleted (cdc_flag = D) account change record means for kept history; the sole member names that the question is open, so L1.history's 'nothing is overwritten' guarantee is not claimed for deleted rows.

Constructed scenarios reach the same account attributes as received records through their own separately labeled (ce.-prefixed) handoffs, never through the raw.-prefixed ones, and the containment invariant confines them to changing an account number the received records already carry, never introducing a new one -- which is what L1.constructed-scenarios requires. No constructed-scenario source is defined for customers in the anchors, so this group covers the account side only.
